conventions.convention: Normal-law results assume AC. N(m,σ²) is the affine image m+σZ of the standard normal with σ≥0; standardization requires σ>0.
Φ(x)=P(Z≤x), and z_q is the unique real satisfying Φ(z_q)=q for q∈(0,1). Normal laws have no atoms, and z_(1-q)=-z_q.

Plans have positive integer total sample size; allocation components may be zero if the declared candidate set permits them. Feasibility includes every selected test, precision, allocation, and resource condition.
The finite search uses a supplied list ordered by nondecreasing total size, preserves its tie order, and certifies none only within that list. Its exact evaluator must terminate on each entry.

The all-size evaluator terminates at every positive integer and decides whether any feasible plan exists at that size. Unbounded search never returns none; full-domain none requires a valid completeness or infeasibility certificate. The output is a size, not an allocation witness.
The one-sided test rejects strictly above z_(1-α), has composite null μ≤μ₀, and targets the positive shift δ>0. The two-sided test rejects |Z_n|>z_(1-α/2) under the singleton null μ=μ₀.
The oracle impossibility claim concerns deterministic procedures with only individual-size Boolean queries and no additional information distinguishing the oracles; it includes nondecreasing oracles.

load_bearing.statement: Let F⊆D be the plans meeting all selected test, precision, allocation, and resource conditions. The planned sample size is none if F is empty, and otherwise is the least integer in {n(d):d∈F}.

Assume AC. For Z∼N(0,1), Φ(x)=P(Z≤x) is continuous and strictly increasing with limits 0 and 1 at the two infinite endpoints, P(Z=x)=0, and Φ(-x)=1-Φ(x). Each q∈(0,1) has a unique z_q with Φ(z_q)=q, and z_(1-q)=-z_q.
Assume AC. For a positive integer n and mutually independent real random variables with common law N(μ,σ²), σ≥0, the sample mean has law N(μ,σ²/n). If σ>0, √n( X̄_n-μ₀)/σ has law N(√n(μ-μ₀)/σ,1).
Let S⊆N_{≥1} be nonempty. Then there is a unique n_*∈S such that n_*≤n for every n∈S.
For every real x, ⌈x⌉=-⌊-x⌋ is an integer with x≤⌈x⌉ and, for m∈Z, ⌈x⌉≤m iff x≤m. For a≥0, the least positive integer n with n≥a is max{1,⌈a⌉}.

Under AC and the stated independent known-σ normal model, with α,β_II∈(0,1) and δ>0, the upper-tail z-test has size α and power Φ(√n(μ-μ₀)/σ-z_(1-α)). Its least positive size attaining power 1-β_II at μ₀+δ is max{1,⌈(σ/δ)² max{0,z_(1-α)+z_(1-β_II)}²⌉}.
Under AC and the stated independent known-variance normal model, rejecting |Z_n|>c_α with c_α=z_(1-α/2) has size α. At μ=μ₀+δ, δ∈R, its rejection probability is 1-Φ(c_α-λ)+Φ(-c_α-λ), where λ=√n δ/σ.

Given the planning specification and an exact terminating feasibility evaluator at every positive size, either search positive integers in ascending order, search through a supplied valid finite completeness bound, or return none using a supplied valid all-size infeasibility proof.

Inspect the supplied finite candidate list in nondecreasing size order using its exact terminating evaluator; return the first feasible plan with its size, or none if every entry fails, including immediate none for an empty list.
